notes: Account summary: RollingWave is a mid-market product analytics SaaS (B2B) building an in-app assistant + doc search. Evaluated Redwood Hosted API during a 4-week trial; moving to evaluation for Dedicated reserved capacity for production (data isolation + predictable latency)

Hosted trial highlights (weeks 1-4): avg QPS observed = 12 req/s; peak observed burst = 160 req/s during Monday morning syncs; steady-state concurrency 3-6; instantaneous concurrency spikes to ~30 during onboarding flows
Token mix from trace logs: average prompt tokens = 130, average generation tokens = 320; 18% of calls are long-context (>=2k tokens), 62% responses streamed; token ratio prompt:generated ~1:2.5

Performance SLA target: product team requests p95 generation <150ms (currently p95 on hosted = 210ms for 'gpt-like' open model), 99th <400ms. Critical for in-app assistant UX and real-time reranking in search results

Throughput projections (finance / product): baseline production QPS target = 25 req/s (month 1), expected growth 3x over 12 months; peak planning target = 200 req/s to cover seasonal/onboarding spikes

Preliminary Dedicated sizing recommendation (from SE): start with 4 A100-80GB equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool with autoscale burst to 8 for peaks; expected sustained token throughput ~90M tokens/day at baseline; burst capacity to 300M tokens/day with autoscale
Batching & cache strategy: enable prefix/KV cache for repeated user sessions (estimated 20% token savings) and configure continuous batching for background reranking jobs to reduce unit cost

POC acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 150ms on representative 70/30 traffic split (interactive vs batch), sustained throughput of 25 req/s for 72h with <1% error rate, cost forecast within 15% of worksheet estimate

Security & compliance path: RollingWave requires SSO (SAML), SOC2 report, KMS integration for keys, and audit log retention for 1 year. Security team had one open question about egress rules in VPC deployment (ticket SEC-1892)

Commercials: initial pricing sensitivity — CFO wants a committed reserved price that reduces per-token unit cost by >=20% vs hosted list. Finance asked for 3 pricing scenarios: conservative (no autoscale), baseline (start+burst), aggressive (autoscale + geo fallback).
